how_to_use_as_a_landing_gate: python -X utf8 live_checks/run_hermes_suite_r1.py --selftest   (defaults to the live authoritative tip; pass --ref <candidate-sha> to gate a candidate). Exit 0 = harness collects and runs, 3 = gate red, 4 = self-test red, 7/8 = refused for an unsafe work dir or a bad export. It never writes into the repo and never pushes a ref.

r1_candidate_retrospective.reading: this is the candidate the commander declined to land: 22 discovered files, 2 collection errors, and harness_executed=0 with passed=0 and failed=0 - a run that looks like a summary line but executes nothing. The gate names 4 failing checks and exits 3, so the defect is caught before landing rather than after.

arithmetic_reconciliation.note: both trees collect the same 58 harness tests and the same whole-suite total; what differs is that 2 of the 22 files in the r1 tree cannot import, so its run aborts at collection and executes 0 - collected equality is exactly why a collected-count alone is not a gate

verdict_derivation: derived_ok = and(checks); every value in checks compares readings taken from the two run receipts (their arms blocks), so the verdict cannot be reached by writing a token
